clock_fraction_45: Czech THREE QUARTERS toward the coming hour: "třičtvrtě na devět" == 08:45
(bare_quarter_to + toward_hour_12h; "na" is the toward connector, see
marker_na.voc).  Citation: Internetová jazyková příručka (ÚJČ AV ČR),
"Vyjadřování času": "tři čtvrtě na sedm" == 6.45; the spaced spelling the
authority writes is joined onto this one by the number fold.

marker_bc: The Internetová jazyková příručka of the Ústav pro jazyk český lists both
the secular "př. n. l." (před naším letopočtem) and the Christian "př. Kr."
(před Kristem) among the purely graphic abbreviations
(https://prirucka.ujc.cas.cz/?id=780). The spaced form is the recommended

marker_for_date: "na" + accusative marks the time a thing is meant for: "na zítra", "na pátek".
Source: cs.wiktionary.org, entry "na": "(na + akuzativ) vyjadřuje časové
určení" (Na podzim padá listí ze stromů).
marker_half: Czech period noun "half" for "first/second half of <year>" (half_period).
"polovina": Slovník spisovného jazyka českého (ÚJČ AV ČR) -- "polovina" =
jedna ze dvou stejných částí celku ("první polovina roku").
"půl" is the bound/prefixal form kept for the clock half-hour path.
marker_last: Czech "last/previous" determiner, the full hard-adjective paradigm (vzor
"mladý").  "v minulém týdnu", "v minulém měsíci" and "v minulém roce" are
locative, and the instrumental "minulým" appears in date framings, so the
whole paradigm is listed rather than the three forms that were here.
Internetová jazyková příručka, ÚJČ AV ČR -- skloňování přídavných jmen tvrdých.
marker_na: Czech toward-hour connector "na" ("onto"): the fraction names how far the
clock has advanced INTO the hour that is coming, so the hour spoken after
"na" is the NEXT one -- "čtvrt na devět" == a quarter onto the ninth ==
08:15, "tři čtvrtě na devět" == three quarters onto the ninth == 08:45.
This is NOT the subtractive "do"/"pred" reading (clock_dir_to.voc), which
counts backwards from the named hour; the two must not be merged.  The same
construction is spelled with "na" in Slovak, Belarusian and Ukrainian.

i.e. the "to/up to" of a numeric or calendar range.
